newsitem.title: UK: BOXING-"PRINCE" NASEEM STOPS JOHNSON TO UNIFY TITLES.
newsitem.headline: BOXING-"PRINCE" NASEEM STOPS JOHNSON TO UNIFY TITLES.

text.p: Britain's "Prince" Naseem Hamed stopped American Tom "Boom Boom" Johnson in the eighth round to unify two featherweight world titles on Saturday.

American referee Rudy Battle stopped the fight after Naseem, the WBO champion, unleashed a ferocious onslaught from all angles culminating in a right uppercut which left Johnson, the IBF titleholder, unable to get up off the canvas.
"You're looking at a legend soon to be," Naseem told reporters ringside after the win. Naseem is the first boxer to fell the American who had defended his title no less than 11 times.

Asked what he intended to do about the other titles in the division, Naseem said: "I am going to bring them back to Britain." Naseem was hoping a win would silence his critics and make the Americans who dominate the sport sit up and pay attention.
After a tentative start as both fighters sized up the other and jabbed from distance, Naseem closed in towards the end of the third round to try to make good his pre-bout prediction.
"I said the third round, but what can I say. Boom Boom is a great fighter," 22-year old Naseem said. "Total respect to the boy."
The 32-year old veteran soaked up the blows despite looking increasingly wobbly, and fought back in the next two rounds to land some heavy rights as Naseem lunged in for the big hit.

In the fourth round, Naseem, sporting his usual leopard skin shorts with Prince written in gold across the front, wobbled his legs in a humiliating impression of the shaky American and stood back to pick his punches, allowing Johnson to regain some of his composure.
"I was biding my time," Naseem said.
By the sixth round Naseem stepped up a gear and began slinging blows from all angles while Johnson looked noticeably heavier on his feet and his punch combinations appeared slow and loose.

Johnson maintained an orthodox style and led with the left throughout whereas Naseem switched leading hands, stood square on and even came at the American from the sides before flooring him with his trademark efficiency.
"I thank Allah for giving me strength," Naseem said.
